note_claims.claim: Routine lithium monitoring review for bipolar affective disorder.
Patient reports stable mood and good energy.
Patient denies racing thoughts or overspending.
Patient has no missed lithium doses.
Patient took ibuprofen for back pain for 3–4 days last week.
Patient has no diarrhoea, vomiting, unsteadiness, or confusion.
Patient has a long-standing fine tremor in both hands, which is unchanged.
Patient has good fluid intake.
Patient is prescribed Priadel (lithium carbonate) 800 mg twice daily.
Patient has no known drug allergies.
Fine tremor of both hands is present and unchanged.
Gait is steady.
Lithium level last month was 0.7 mmol/L (12-hour post-dose), which is in range.
eGFR is 74, which is stable.
Thyroid function and calcium are normal.
Diagnosis is bipolar affective disorder on lithium.
Lithium level was in range last month.
Recent NSAID use poses a risk of raised lithium level.
Possible early signs of hypomanic relapse reported by wife.
Continue Priadel 800 mg at night.
Repeat lithium level in 1 week (12 hours post-dose) due to NSAID exposure.
Lithium level monitoring will return to every three months after the recheck.
Patient should avoid NSAIDs and use paracetamol for back pain.
Patient will be informed of sleep and energy concerns by the community mental health team.
Patient must keep a sleep diary and contact the care coordinator if sleeping less than five hours for two consecutive nights.
If vomiting, diarrhoea, coarse tremor, unsteadiness, or confusion occurs, the patient must stop lithium and seek an urgent lithium level or attend A&E.
Patient should avoid dehydration, especially in hot weather.

transcript_facts.fact: Clinician greeted Mr Fairweather-Okoro and asked about his wife.
Patient identified herself as Adaeze.
Relative greeted the clinician.
Clinician asked if it was okay for Adaeze to stay.
Patient confirmed she was okay with staying.
Clinician initiated the routine lithium review.
Patient reported mood has been steady and work is going well.
Clinician asked about sleep.
Patient reported feeling fine.
Relative reported the patient has been sleeping five hours or less this last week and has been talking a lot more, starting lots of projects.
Patient reported feeling well and having loads of energy.
Clinician asked if the patient was having racing thoughts or spending more money than usual.
Patient denied racing thoughts or overspending.
Clinician asked if the patient was on Priadel, 800 milligrams at night.
Patient confirmed she is on Priadel, 800 milligrams at night.
Clinician asked about missed doses.
Patient confirmed she has never missed a dose.
Clinician asked about other recent medicines, including those from the chemist.
Patient initially stated she took ibuprofen, but corrected herself to naproxen, which her brother gave her.
Clinician asked how many days she took the medication.
Patient stated she took it for three or four days.
Clinician noted that anti-inflammatory painkillers can raise lithium levels and asked about diarrhoea or vomiting.
Patient denied diarrhoea or vomiting.
Clinician asked about feeling unsteady on feet or muddled.
Patient denied feeling unsteady on feet or muddled.
Clinician asked about a change in tremor.
Patient reported no change in tremor, stating it is the same little shake she has always had.
Clinician asked if the patient was drinking plenty of fluids.
Patient confirmed she has a big water bottle at work.
Clinician asked about other medicines and allergies.
Patient stated she has no other medicines and no allergies.
Clinician reviewed blood tests: lithium level last month was 0.7 mmol/L (12-hour post-dose), eGFR is 74 (stable), and thyroid and calcium are normal.
Patient responded with 'Good'.
Clinician examined hands and noted a fine tremor in both hands, which is the same as before, and confirmed the patient was walking steadily.
Patient responded with 'Okay'.
Clinician planned to recheck the lithium level in one week (12 hours after the evening dose) due to naproxen exposure, and then return to every three months.
Patient agreed to the plan.
Clinician advised the patient not to take ibuprofen or naproxen, suggesting paracetamol for back pain.
Patient acknowledged the advice.

Clinician planned to inform the community mental health team, ask the patient to keep a sleep diary, and instruct them to contact the care coordinator or clinician if they sleep less than five hours for two nights running.
Relative stated she would keep an eye on the patient.

Clinician instructed the patient to continue Priadel at the same dose and provided safety-netting advice: if vomiting, diarrhoea, coarse shaking, unsteadiness, or confusion occurs, the patient must stop lithium and seek an urgent lithium level or go to A&E.
Patient acknowledged the safety instructions.
Clinician advised the patient to try not to get dehydrated, especially in hot weather.
Patient acknowledged the advice and thanked the doctor.
